metadata.description: Supplemental host-plant evidence extracted from PDFs retrieved after the GPT-Pro seed was generated.
sources: Muriel, S. B., Montoya, J., Restrepo, A. & Munoz, J. 2011. Nuevos registros de plantas hospederas y disponibilidad de recursos para mariposas Ithomiini, en agroecosistemas de cafe colombianos. Actualidades Biologicas 33(95): 275-285. DOI: 10.17533/udea.acbi.14326.
McClure, M. & Elias, M. 2016. Unravelling the role of host plant expansion in the diversification of a Neotropical butterfly genus. BMC Evolutionary Biology 16:128. DOI: 10.1186/s12862-016-0701-5.

Hill, R. I., Elias, M., Dasmahapatra, K. K., Jiggins, C. D. et al. 2012. Host plant use and ecological differentiation in Mechanitis butterflies, with Table 3 host records for Mechanitis messenoides and M. mazaeus in eastern Ecuador.
Melo, D. H. A. & Freitas, A. V. L. 2023. Immature stages of Mechanitis lysimnia nesaea (Nymphalidae: Danainae: Ithomiini). Tropical Lepidoptera Research 33(2): 79-85.
PLOS Biology 2026 Mechanitis mimicry study; outdoor insectary stocks used Solanum quitoense for oviposition and larval rearing.

Anteparra, M. E., Ayvar, J. C. & Granados, L. B. 2011. Algunos aspectos sobre la biologia de Mechanitis polymnia proceriformis Bryk, 1953 asociado con la Cocona (Solanum sessiliflorum Dunal) en Tingo Maria. Aporte Santiaguino 4(1): 64-74. DOI: 10.32911/as.2011.v4.n1.530.
notes: Muriel et al. Table 3 records are field-collected eggs/larvae/pupae reared in the laboratory from coffee agroecosystems in Fredonia, Antioquia, Colombia.
McClure & Elias records summarize field host-use context reported for the four Melinaea species studied; experimental host-acceptance-only results are not added as default host associations here.

Mechanitis messenoides records added from Hill et al. 2012 are treated as species-level direct field records where plant identity was exact, and as needs-check records where Hill et al. used cf. or naranjilla-like unresolved plant categories.

Older catalogue rows under Mechanitis mazaeus that explicitly refer to ssp. messenoides or ssp. deceptus are duplicated as modern-taxonomy remap candidates for M. messenoides rather than used to copy all M. mazaeus or M. polymnia hosts.

Solanum quitoense is retained for M. messenoides with a husbandry caveat and needs-check/default-hidden support category because the strongest exact-species evidence is oviposition/rearing in outdoor insectary stocks, not a clean wild field-host record.
Anteparra et al. 2011 was retrieved by DOI and saved outside the repo at /home/franz/Documents/CodeProjs/hostplant source PDFs/unpaywall_10.32911_as.2011.v4.n1.530.pdf.

records.source_citation: PLOS Biology 2026 Mechanitis mimicry study; outdoor insectary husbandry methods
